actives.name: Naive/unmodified MSC- or adipose-derived exosomes (EVs)
actives.note: A purified/isolated exosome preparation is mechanistically the cleanest option but cost-prohibitive to purify at nasal-spray scale. The secretome retains this fraction without the purification cost.

actives.name: Engineered or cargo-loaded EVs (e.g. miRNA-, BDNF-, or drug-loaded exosomes)
actives.note: Excluded for now — zero human intranasal precedent, rodent/in vitro models only. Inherits naive EVs' undefined delivery mechanism plus an unvalidated loading step, with no regulatory precedent for the combination-product question.

actives.name: MSC secretome / conditioned medium (cell-free)
actives.note: Intended active is the exosome fraction of the secretome. Full exosome purification is cost-prohibitive at consumer nasal-spray scale, so the product is unpurified MSC secretome that retains the exosome fraction rather than a purified isolate. Remaining secretome components (soluble growth factors and cytokines) may contribute additively; this is not established and is not relied on for the core mechanism.

actives.name: Intranasal insulin
actives.note: Highest four-axis score of any candidate compared — tracked as a benchmark, not adopted. Not a regenerative/tissue-repair active; would not support the focus candidate's mechanistic framing. SNIFF (NCT01767909), n≈240, RCT, 12 months, in the target population (MCI/Alzheimer's).

actives.name: Intranasal oxytocin
actives.note: Exceeds the focus candidate on mechanism, manufacturability, and regulatory tractability — tracked as a benchmark, not adopted. Evidence is the most genuinely mixed in the comparison: a well-run RCT (NEJM 2021) found no significant cognitive/social effect.

actives.name: NAD⁺ precursors (NMN, nicotinamide riboside)
actives.note: Excluded — its one strong axis (manufacturability, as an unregulated supplement) evaporates once a cognitive-function disease claim forces reclassification as a drug. No intranasal human trial of any kind was found; oral cognitive evidence is itself weak or null.

excipients.name: Monobasic potassium phosphate / dibasic sodium phosphate
excipients.precedent: IID nasal MONOBASIC POTASSIUM PHOSPHATE; TOSYMRA (NDA 210884); SPRIX (NDA 022382)
excipients.tradeoff: 10 mM stays well below the ~0.13 M threshold where a buffer starts overriding nasal pH (Washington et al. 2000), but the molarity itself is transferred from a lyophilisate study, not derived for this product.

excipients.name: Sodium chloride
excipients.precedent: IID nasal SOLUTION 330 mg / LIQUID 7.4 mg/mL; TOSYMRA; calcitonin-salmon nasal spray
excipients.tradeoff: Level is open pending the stabilizer decision, since the stabilizer itself contributes osmolality; counter-ion identity (Na⁺ vs K⁺) may matter more to vesicle stability than a tonicity calculation captures.

excipients.name: Trehalose (25 mM)
excipients.precedent: no precedent — regulatory risk (IID: intradermal, subcutaneous only; no nasal-route entry)
excipients.tradeoff: Deepest EV-specific stabilization evidence of any excipient considered (Bosch 2016, Görgens 2022, Charoenviriyakul 2018), but would need a nasal-route safety qualification package.

excipients.name: Mannitol
excipients.tradeoff: Only sugar/polyol with nasal precedent and a stated max potency, but a crystallizing bulking agent — a weaker lyoprotectant for a membrane particle than an amorphous disaccharide; no EV-specific data found.

excipients.name: Human serum albumin (0.2%)
excipients.precedent: no precedent — regulatory risk (IID: intravenous, oral only; no nasal-route entry)
excipients.tradeoff: Suppresses the plastic-surface EV adsorption loss Görgens (2022) measured within minutes, but carries no nasal-route precedent at all.

excipients.name: HEPES (25 mM)
excipients.precedent: no precedent — regulatory risk (absent from the IID entirely, by any route)
excipients.tradeoff: Buffer base of PBS-HAT, the lead published EV-stabilization buffer (Görgens 2022), but has no US excipient precedent whatsoever.

excipients.name: Sucrose (5%)
excipients.precedent: no precedent — regulatory risk (IID: 10 other routes incl. IV, ophthalmic, oral; no nasal-route entry)
excipients.tradeoff: Improves EV colloidal stability on freeze-thaw and supports a lyophilisate stable 6 months at 40°C (Trenkenschuh 2022), but zero nasal-route precedent.

excipients.name: Poloxamer 188 (0.02%)
excipients.precedent: no precedent — regulatory risk (IID: 7 other routes incl. IV, ophthalmic, intratympanic; no nasal-route entry)
excipients.tradeoff: The single most effective published EV colloidal-stability agent (Trenkenschuh 2022), but zero nasal-route precedent.

excipients.name: Polysorbate 80 (0.01% w/v)
excipients.precedent: IID nasal SPRAY, METERED, 0.1 mg/1 mL
excipients.tradeoff: The nasal-precedented stand-in for poloxamer 188, but its CMC is in the low micromolar range — even 0.01% sits above it, the same surfactant-above-CMC property that disqualified DDM, unmeasured against these vesicles.

excipients.name: Hypromellose 2910 (5 mPa·s)
excipients.precedent: IID nasal SPRAY/SPRAY METERED, 1 mg/1 mL; seen in azelastine ANDAs
excipients.tradeoff: Deliberately deferred, not chosen: added viscosity coarsens the plume and risks the <4.6% olfactory deposition fraction the product depends on; cellulose-polymer/EV adsorption compatibility is untested.

excipients.name: n-Dodecyl β-D-maltoside (DDM / Intravail)
excipients.precedent: IID nasal SPRAY; TOSYMRA (NDA 210884) at 0.2% w/v
excipients.tradeoff: ~23× its own CMC and roughly 500 mol detergent per mol lipid at this product's target particle concentration — would be expected to dissolve the vesicle active.

excipients.name: Chitosan
excipients.precedent: no precedent — regulatory risk (absent from the nasal IID and from all 694 nasal labels)
excipients.tradeoff: Frequently proposed in the delivery literature as a nasal permeation enhancer, but its cationic, membrane-interacting mode of action raises the same vesicle-disruption question as every other enhancer here.

excipients.name: Benzalkonium chloride (BAC)
excipients.precedent: the dominant nasal preservative, 535 of 694 nasal labels
excipients.tradeoff: Ciliotoxic at nasal use concentrations (Riechelmann et al. 2004, p<0.0001); a cationic surfactant in continuous contact with a vesicle active for the whole in-use life of the bottle.

excipients.name: Plain PBS (as vehicle)
excipients.precedent: sodium chloride and sodium phosphate both have nasal precedent
excipients.tradeoff: Severe EV recovery loss within days on storage and within minutes on dilution (Görgens et al. 2022); ranked below potassium phosphate for EV stability (Trenkenschuh et al. 2022).

excipients.name: Citrate buffer
excipients.precedent: IID nasal citrate entries; TOSYMRA uses citric acid monohydrate
excipients.tradeoff: Good nasal precedent, but buffers to pH 5–6 — the acidic region associated with EV aggregation and vesicle fusion (Trenkenschuh et al. 2022). Precedent for the wrong pH.

presentation.shelf_life: unpublished by Signal; site meta description claims "shelf-stable" but no storage temperature or duration appears anywhere on the page (fetched 2026-09-03)
presentation.user_steps: single actuation from a 10 mL multi-dose metered spray, no reconstitution
presentation.verdict: unsupported as currently specified — EVs in aqueous buffer without a nasal-precedented stabilizer lose recoverable particles within minutes to days (Görgens et al. 2022); the "shelf-stable" claim has no formulation or storage-condition evidence behind it.

presentation.shelf_life: 6 months at 40°C for particle size and concentration (Trenkenschuh et al. 2022) — the only published route to anything resembling "shelf-stable" for this active; not tested for this specific formulation
presentation.cold_chain: not required for storage per the cited lyophilisate data; unconfirmed for this product
presentation.user_steps: reconstitute the lyophilized cake with diluent before use, then spray — an added step versus the currently marketed single-actuation format
presentation.verdict: best-evidenced route to a genuine stability claim, but presentation-and-device.md (device, fill, reconstitution spec) does not exist yet, and it changes the stabilizer decision from a cryoprotectant-in-solution to a lyophilisate cake.

presentation.shelf_life: consensus long-term storage condition for EV preparations at −80°C (Ahmadian et al. 2024, cited via sgl-001-spec.md); one freeze-thaw cycle costs 23–36% of particles
presentation.cold_chain: required — an unbroken −80°C freezer chain from manufacture through point of use
presentation.user_steps: thaw before each use; repeated freeze-thaw is destructive, so single-use aliquots would be needed rather than a multi-dose bottle
presentation.verdict: ruled out for a consumer multi-dose product — the cold-chain requirement and per-cycle particle loss are incompatible with a bottle used over multiple days and with the site's own "shelf-stable" framing.
